newsitem.title: ROMANIA: FORECAST-Romania reserves $2.0 bln by June or July.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Romania reserves $2.0 bln by June or July.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) foreign exchange reserves are expected to almost double to some $2.0 billion in June or July from the present $1.1 billion, BNR governor Mugur Isarescu said on Monday.

"The BNR's reserves are seen rising to $1.4-$1.5 billion early in May and reach about $2.0 billion in June or July, if one considers the amounts we expect to get from the IMF and the European Union as well as our purchases from the local foreign exchange market," Isarescu told a news conference.

This year, Romania expects to get about $400 million from the International Monetary Fund and 70 million Ecus from the EU. The IMF Board will discuss the issue of restoring loans to Romania on Tuesday, one day earlier than previously announced.
The expected $400 million IMF funds, designed to underpin market reforms would be disbursed in tranches of $80 million.
Latest data put Romania's total reserve assets, including some 88 tonnes of gold, at $2.7 billion in February, with the BNR's own reserves of $697.7 million.
Isarescu said a dollar-heavy interbank market had determined the BNR to soak the excess of dollars in order to prevent a sharp appreciation of the local leu currency.
"Over the past six weeks the BNR bought about $250 million from the local market," he said.

"We have to support the greenback, having in mind the large inflows of hard currency on our market," said Isarescu. "Those inflows came from exports repatriation and higher direct and portfolio investments in Romania over the past months."

Foreign direct investments in Romania rose by 35 percent in the first quarter this year against the same period of 1996, pushing to $2.3 billion the overall figure of investments in Romania since the 1989 fall of communism.
"We have certain signals saying we will buy about $50-$60 million from the market this week," Isarescu said.
He said tougher monetary policies earlier this year and the liberalisation of the foreign exchange market had triggered a smooth functioning of currency markets.
"The market is functioning well and is liquid. There are no big fluctuations of the leu's exchange rate. Hard currency demand is satisfied fast," he said.
The leu has traded fairly stable over the past weeks near 7,040/100 to the dollar, recovering smoothly after a plunge to 9,000 in mid-February from about 4,100 in the New Year.
